transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um… I guess what brings me in is my eating has gotten really out of hand, especially in the evenings. I’ll stop after work or order takeout, and it’s not just a normal dinner. It’ll be like a family-size order—enough for several people—and then I’ll still go by the store and get chips or something from the bakery, like cookies or pastries, and I’ll tell myself it’s just to have around.

But then I get home and I eat most of it myself. Sometimes it feels like I barely even notice what I’m doing until I look down and so much of it is gone. It’s embarrassing to say out loud, but that’s really why I’m here. It keeps happening, and I’m worried because it feels bigger than just “I ate too much.”
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I’m… not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I know what you’re asking, like whether I do something on purpose afterward to “undo” it. I don’t think I have a clear pattern like that that I could point to and say, yes, I do that.

Afterward I mostly feel awful and ashamed, and I might tell myself I’m going to be “good” the next day, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing as what you mean by fasting or compensating. I’m not sitting there with a plan, like, “Now I have to make up for this in this specific way.” It’s more like I feel guilty and want the whole thing to disappear.
During these times when you eat a lot, do you feel like you can’t control how much you’re eating or that you can’t stop once you start?

Yes. That’s probably the part that scares me the most, honestly. It’s not just that I decide to have too much and then regret it. It feels like once I start, something kind of… flips.

I can literally be thinking, Taylor, stop. Put it away. Close the container. You don’t even want this anymore. And at the same time my hands are still opening the next box, or going back to the bag, or taking another thing out of the carton. It’s like there’s a split between the part of me that knows I should stop and the part of me that’s still doing it.

And I know that sounds strange, because obviously it is me doing it, but in the moment it doesn’t feel like I’m fully in charge. I’ll tell myself, “Okay, just one more,” and then it’s not one more. Or I’ll think, “I’ll put the rest in the fridge,” and then I keep standing there eating it before I even get a plate or sit down properly. It’s this awful, automatic feeling, like I’m watching myself keep going and I can’t get the brakes to work.
Do these eating episodes happen even when you're not physically hungry, or do they usually start because you're very hungry after skipping meals or dieting?

A lot of the time, it’s not because I’m physically hungry. That’s what feels so confusing and, honestly, kind of humiliating. I can have eaten a normal dinner already—like a real dinner, not just a tiny snack—and then later I’ll still find myself going back into the kitchen, opening the fridge, looking through the freezer or the pantry shelves, checking what’s there like I’m searching for something.

And it doesn’t feel like, “Oh, my stomach is empty, I need food.” It’s more like… food is there, and I get this feeling that I have to keep going with it, or finish things, or find the next thing. I’ll stand there looking through containers or bags even though I know I’m not hungry in the normal sense. Sometimes I’ve just eaten, and I’m still opening cabinets like there’s something I’m supposed to complete. It’s really upsetting because my body isn’t asking for it, but I still go looking.
Have these eating episodes caused you significant distress or affected your daily life, like making it hard to focus on work, social activities, or other responsibilities?

Yes, it has. I mean, I try to tell myself it’s just something that happens at home and then I can sort of contain it, but that’s not really true anymore.

After it happens, I get so ashamed and preoccupied that the rest of the evening is basically gone. I’ll have had plans to do yoga, even just a short routine, or go outside and do some gardening chores, pull weeds, water things, whatever small thing needed doing, and instead I just… don’t. I sit there thinking about what I ate, or I’m cleaning up evidence of it, or I’m telling myself how disgusting it was, and then suddenly it’s too late or I’m too embarrassed and drained to do anything.

And socially, yes, it’s affected that too. I’ve pretty much stopped inviting people over. I used to have people come by more casually, but now I worry about what’s in the kitchen, or whether I’ll feel out of control later, or honestly whether someone will notice things. And after one of those episodes I don’t want anyone near me. I don’t want to answer messages, I don’t want to make plans, I don’t want to be seen.

So yes, it does interfere. Maybe not in a dramatic way every single time, but it shrinks my life. It makes my evenings smaller, and it keeps me from doing normal things I used to do without thinking so much about them.
When these episodes happen, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal, like you're rushing through the food without really noticing it?

Yes. Very much so. It’s not like normal eating at all, where I’m tasting things or deciding, “Oh, I want another bite.” It’s fast—embarrassingly fast.

A lot of the time I’m not even sitting down properly. I’ll be standing at the dining room table with stuff spread around me, like something from the microwave, boxes open, containers out, wrappers or packaging there, and I’m just… moving from one thing to the next. I’ll swallow a bite and my hand is already reaching for the next one before I’ve even really registered what I just ate.

And I barely taste it. That’s the part that makes me feel awful afterward, because it’s not even like I enjoyed it in a normal way. It’s more like rushing through it, almost frantic. I’ll realize I’ve eaten a lot and I don’t even have a clear memory of the flavor or whether I liked it. It’s just bite, swallow, reach, bite, swallow, reach. Like I’m trying to get through it before some part of me can stop it.
Do you often eat alone during these episodes because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yes. I really do. I actually plan it around being alone, which feels awful to admit out loud.

If my husband is awake and around, I’m much more likely to hold it together, or at least pretend I’m just getting a normal snack. But if he’s gone to bed, that’s when I’ll start going back into the kitchen. I listen for whether he’s asleep, or I wait until the house is quiet. And with the contractors we’ve had around, I won’t do it while they’re there. I’ll wait until they leave, because the idea of someone seeing me eat like that is… I mean, I would be mortified.

Especially because during the day at work I’m so controlled. I’m a supervisor, so I’m used to looking like I have things handled—being organized, appropriate, professional. I don’t want anyone seeing this completely different version of me, where I can put away so much food in a short time. It feels like it would expose something really shameful. So yes, I eat alone on purpose because I’m embarrassed by how much it is.
After these eating episodes, do you often feel disgusted with yourself, guilty, or upset about what you've eaten?

I mean… I’m not really sure how to answer that in a clean yes-or-no way. I do feel bad afterward, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s always the same feeling each time.

Sometimes it’s more like this heavy embarrassment, like I just want to erase the whole thing and not think about it. Other times I’m upset with myself because I feel like I should have been able to stop or make a different choice. But I don’t know if “disgusted” is exactly the word every time. It’s hard to separate what I actually feel from what I tell myself I should feel, if that makes sense.

I just know that afterward I’m usually not okay. I’m not relaxed or satisfied. I’m sort of sitting there with this awful awareness of what happened, and I don’t really want anyone to see me right then.
On average, how often do these eating episodes happen? Would you say they occur at least once a week?

Yes. Definitely at least once a week.

I actually started trying to track it in a journal because I kept telling myself maybe it wasn’t happening that often, or maybe I was exaggerating it in my head. But when I look back through the pages, there has barely been a week in the last several months where there wasn’t at least one night like that. And honestly, most weeks it isn’t just once. Most weeks it happens several times.

It’s hard to say that because part of me wants to soften it, like, “Well, it depends on the week,” and it does a little, but if I’m being honest, yes—this is a regular thing. It’s not some rare slip that happens once in a while. It’s been showing up week after week.
